results.content: # Explainability and Interpretability in Concept and Data Drift: A Systematic Literature Review Against this backdrop, our systematic review aims to consolidate current research on explainability and interpretability with a focus on concept and data drift. explainability; explainable AI; interpretability; interpretable AI; concept drift; data drift :   **Trend**: How has research on explainability and interpretability for concept and data drift evolved over time? :   **Online Adaptation of XAI:** How are traditional XAI methods—designed for static models—adapted to online learning environments to maintain interpretability under concept/data drift? (Data Drift): It is a specific type of drift concerning changes in the distribution of the input data over time, without necessarily altering the underlying concept that maps inputs to outputs. Data drift occurs when the marginal feature distribution changes; i.e., there exist times (𝑡1,𝑡2) such that Given a data stream (𝑆 ={(𝑥𝑡,𝑦𝑡)}∞𝑡=1), drift denotes any time-dependent departure of the stream’s data-generating distribution from the one that prevailed when a predictive model was trained.

results.title: Transforming Healthcare with State-of-the-Art Medical-LLMs
results.content: Medical Large Language Models (Med-LLMs) serve as transformative tools that enhance clinical practice through applications in decision support, documentation, and diagnostics. Medical large language models (Med-LLM); AI in healthcare; natural language processing (NLP) in medicine; fine-tuning medical LLMs; retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in medicine; multi-modal learning in healthcare; explainability and transparency in medical AI; FDA regulations for AI in medicine; evaluation and benchmarking of medical large language models Large Language Models (LLMs) have garnered the majority of attention in healthcare AI research due to their unparalleled ability to process, generate, and contextualize natural language. While numerous surveys published in 2024–2025 [24,27–31] explore the development, architecture, and clinical applications of Medical Large Language Models (Med-LLMs), a critical gap remains in evaluating these models from the perspective of real-world deployment readiness. Large Language Models (LLMs) are advanced AI systems built on deep learning techniques and trained on vast collections of text data to comprehend and produce natural language.
